We need to apply template 1679747 to the initial molecule SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2

We have template mapping from previous step: mapped_rxn shows reaction: O=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1 . [Li][CH2:1][Si](C)(C)C >> [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1

So template is a Wittig-type? Reactants: a carbonyl (O= C) attached to aromatic rings with methoxy groups, and a LiCH2Si(C)(C)C (a silyl carbanion). Product is an alkene (CH2= C attached to aromatic rings). So applying template to target molecule (the product) should give precursors: the carbonyl compound and the silyl carbanion.

Our target molecule is C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2 which matches product: CH2= C(aryl1)(aryl2) where each aryl is phenyl with OMe substituent at para? Actually structure: C=C(Ph-OMe)Ph-OMe. So yes.

Thus applying template should give two precursors: the carbonyl (O= C(aryl1)(aryl2)?) Wait carbonyl in template: O=[C:2]([c:3]... ) [c:11]... So carbonyl attached to two aryl groups (both methoxy phenyl). So carbonyl is a diaryl ketone with methoxy groups: O=C(Ar1)(Ar2) where each Ar is phenyl-OMe (para). So SMILES: O=C(c1ccc(OC)cc1)c2ccc(OC)cc2 . That's benzophenone with methoxy groups.

Second precursor: [Li][CH2:1][Si](C)(C)C i.e., LiCH2SiMe3? Actually Si(C)(C)C is Si with three methyl groups (trimethylsilyl). So SMILES: [Li][CH2][Si](C)(C)C . Might need proper SMILES: [Li][CH2][Si](C)(C)C . That's the silyl carbanion.

Thus apply_template should return list of precursors combos: each combination is list of SMILES strings. Likely only one combination.

We can verify by using apply_template tool.
